about: Round 734. Every row of public.f1_driver_standings (3,095 rows, seasons 1950 to 2025) as read on 2026-09-30 through the Supabase MCP, checked against formula1.com (the official results archive: the final drivers standings page and the race winners page of each season) and the Jolpica F1 API (the documented dataset, maintained successor of the Ergast API, which the table was imported from). ESPN and Motor Sport magazine's database are the third sources that settled every disagreement. Wikipedia is not a source here.

Each row is [id, driver_id, driver_name, constructor_id, constructor_name, position, points, wins, status] in its state AFTER the Round 734 migration. A row's two sources are its season's src pair (formula1.com standings, Jolpica), and its wins are also counted from formula1.com's race winners (winsSrc). A corrected row's sources are in changes. The top three of every season are repeated in top3 with their own source pair.

Status: verified (position, points and wins agree with formula1.com and one more source; a scoreless unranked row agrees with Jolpica, is absent from formula1.com's points table, and raceStarts names the formula1.com race result that shows he started), corrected (the migration changes it, to the value formula1.com and a second source agree on), filled (the migration inserts it), marked (kept as read because the sources disagree or only one source speaks; notes says which). None is dropped.

Scope. The games read driver_name where position is 1 (the List Quiz F1 champions list), and src/data/f1HLDrivers.ts was baked from the wins column. Names are checked against formula1.com for the top three of every season and for every Fangio row; below the top three the name is Jolpica's. The constructor column is checked for the top three only (it must be a team formula1.com shows him driving that season). Where formula1.com's standings print a different team text from the column, the top3 entry records that text as constructorPrinted, and where Jolpica lists more than one constructor for him that season, the entry records Jolpica's list as constructors; both fields were read on 2026-10-01. A constructorNote says only what those two fields show. A long entrant name beside a short one (Red Bull Racing Renault beside Red Bull) is one team under two names, not a second team, and no note may say otherwise. The table holds no constructors champion, so none is verified here.

tableAtRead holds the per season fingerprints the MCP returned on 2026-09-30: row count, first id, and four md5 digests of the rows. hcore digests driver_id|position|points|wins with - for no position, hname digests driver_id|driver_name, hcons digests driver_id|constructor_id|constructor_name, each over the season's lines ordered by their own md5 and joined with newlines; hidorder digests the driver_ids in id order joined with commas. scripts/simF1Champions.mjs recomputes all four for every season from the rows with the changes reversed and the filled rows removed, and recomputes the migration's 26 season fingerprints the same way, so this record provably describes both the table as read and the table the migration leaves.
